name: Mindelo
subtitle: Mindelo is the port city of São Vicente island.

facts.label: Town status
facts.value: Raised to the rank of vila in 1859

facts.label: Coal port
facts.value: English coal companies set up there and by 1875 Mindelo was considered the largest coaling port in the mid-Atlantic

facts.label: City status
facts.value: Became a city in 1879, with 3,300 inhabitants, 27 streets and 120 oil lamps

facts.label: Position
facts.value: Because of its location and the Porto Grande, Mindelo became a key point in links between Europe and America, with a strong English presence

facts.label: Decline
facts.value: After the golden years of English shipping and the coal trade, the island entered a slow decline from the end of the 19th century

facts.label: Population 2011
facts.value: A port city of 47,000 people (figure given by AP-based report, 2011)

facts.label: Cesária Évora
facts.value: Singer Cesária Évora was born in Mindelo, a port city on São Vicente; she performed for sailors from ships docking there

facts.label: Carnival decline
facts.value: In the 1960s Mindelo carnival declined when the big groups Oriundo and Estrela da Marinha disappeared

facts.label: Carnival revival
facts.value: 1978, the year of Djibla's 'wedding', marks the turning point of post-independence carnival; between 1975 and 1978 the official parade contest was interrupted

parts.text: Mindelo is the port city of São Vicente island. It grew in the 19th century around the Porto Grande harbour and English coal companies, was raised to city status in 1879, and later became known for its bar and carnival culture and as the home of the singer Cesária Évora.
